songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Swinging early‑68 set with epic New Potato and crystal‑clear Dark Star
ai_show_review.blurb: The performance delivers a lively first half and an expansive second, highlighted by soaring New Potato Caboose and a pristine Dark Star. Jerry’s guitar solos are sublime while Bob’s vocal moment adds humor. Overall the band is tight, energetic, and captures the early‑68 vibe at its best.
ai_show_review.review:
On March 29, 1968 at San Francisco’s Carousel Ballroom the Dead rolled out a quintessential early‑68 set that still feels fresh. The first half swings through blues‑rooted numbers like Good Morning Little School Girl and Death Don't Have No Mercy before launching into a crisp Dark Star that many listeners describe as “crystal‑clear.” After a brief break, the second half climbs to a high point with an expansive New Potato Caboose – Jerry’s guitar soaring with sustained, howling tones – followed by a spirited The Other One suite and a haunting Born Cross‑Eyed fragment. Pigpen’s occasional organ grumbles add a tongue‑in‑cheek flavor to Bob’s vocal solo, and the dual‑drummer lineup (Mickey and Bill) provides a solid, almost single‑drum feel that still drives the groove. Across all three recordings the show is praised for its natural pacing, tight transitions, and the matrix recording in particular offers exceptional instrument separation, making this one of the standout early‑68 documents.

For Deadheads hunting an early period gem, this show checks every box: vibrant setlist flow, legendary solos, and a recording quality that lets you hear every nuance. Whether you listen to the Miller matrix or the high‑energy audience tapes, the performance remains a benchmark for the band’s 1968 evolution.

best_recording.reason: Matrix source with crystal‑clear instrument separation, no dropouts, and superb capture of New Potato Caboose and Dark Star.

key_highlights: Epic New Potato Caboose with sublime Jerry solos
Crystal‑clear Dark Star that showcases early‑68 improvisation
Powerful vocal moment from Bob with Pigpen’s humorous organ interjection
Tight dual‑drummer groove; Mickey’s presence confirmed despite single‑drum feel
song_highlights: Sitting On Top Of The World

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers sublime, top‑tier solos on New Potato Caboose and Dark Star, with deep‑throated vocals that anchor the set.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh adds a deep, powerful bass foundation; his spoken quip after Sitting On Top Of The World is noted, though some listeners feel his bass sits low in the mix.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s vocal solo stands out, punctuated by Pigpen humorously cursing his organ during the moment.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart’s drumming is emphasized, providing a solid pulse that many initially mistake for a single‑drummer feel, confirming his presence in this lineup.

must_listen_sequences: Sitting On Top Of The World
